speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; to begin my assessment, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and do you have any history of heart disease or high blood pressure?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture). The history of forceful vomiting following heavy alcohol consumption, followed by choking, coughing, and severe chest pain, is classic for this condition. I am requesting a CT scan with oral contrast and an esophagram to confirm the diagnosis and locate the tear.
